relations.note: Anu is treated as Erra’s father in later learned genealogy.
God-list theology pairs Erra with Mami as his wife.
Nergal’s parentage by Enlil was transferred to Erra after their equation.
Nergal’s parentage by Ninlil was transferred to Erra after their equation.
One transferred Nergal genealogy makes Bēlet-ilī the mother of Erra.
Nergal’s marriage to Laṣ could be transferred to syncretized Erra.
Nergal’s pairing with Admu could be transferred to syncretized Erra.
Nergal’s pairing with Ninšubur could be transferred to syncretized Erra.

relations.myth: Išum serves as Erra’s vanguard and interlocutor
relations.note: Erra appoints Išum as his vanguard during the destructive campaign.

relations.myth: Išum accompanies and channels Erra’s campaign
relations.note: Išum accompanies Erra and redirects his violence toward restoring order.

relations.myth: Išum persuades Erra to end his fury
relations.note: Išum repeatedly rebukes Erra and ultimately calms his destructive rage.

relations.myth: Erra induces Marduk to leave Babylon
relations.note: Erra uses the purported need to purify Marduk’s statue and regalia.

relations.myth: Erra exploits Marduk’s absence from Babylon
relations.note: Erra seizes control and devastates Babylon after its protector departs.

relations.myth: The Seven become Erra’s destructive instruments
relations.note: Anu gives the Seven to Erra as weapons and champions of massacre.

relations.myth: The Seven urge and accompany Erra’s campaign
relations.note: They rouse Erra to battle and accompany his destructive campaign.
Erra invokes Girra’s fire purification to induce Marduk’s withdrawal.
Literary texts and god lists explicitly treat Nergal as another name for Erra.
Erra devastates Uruk and its Ištar-associated dependants without a preserved direct encounter.
Erra threatens to dim Šulpaea’s brilliance in celestial-divinatory language.

relations.myth: Erra’s disorder disrupts the moon god
relations.note: Erra’s catastrophe affects Sîn’s light and regularity without a certain personal encounter.

relations.myth: Erra’s disorder affects justice and cosmic light
relations.note: Erra’s violence disrupts Šamaš’s spheres, though no secure direct dialogue survives.

relations.myth: Erra’s catastrophe disrupts Adad’s agricultural sphere
relations.note: Erra’s disorder engages Adad’s storm and agricultural functions without a secure encounter.

relations.myth: Erra descends and unites with Ereškigal
relations.note: As Nergal’s interchangeable name, Erra becomes Ereškigal’s partner and underworld co-ruler.

relations.myth: Erra confronts Ereškigal in the underworld
relations.note: The Erra-named protagonist breaches underworld protocol and confronts Ereškigal before their union.
Learned theology draws Erra and Ninurta into equivalence through overlapping warrior roles.
Later lists relate or equate Erragal with Erra, though their original identity remains disputed.
